nodes.label: Standard Application Lifecycle statuses
nodes.rationale: Applied, Screening, Interview, TechnicalInterview, FinalInterview, Offer, Accepted, Rejected, Withdrawn, Ghosted; Draft is optional for MVP.

nodes.label: Browser Extension ('I Applied' from LinkedIn job page)
nodes.norm_label: browser extension ('i applied' from linkedin job page)

nodes.label: Email integration (classification -> status suggestion -> user confirmation)
nodes.norm_label: email integration (classification -> status suggestion -> user confirmation)
nodes.rationale: First version prefers user confirmation over automatic status change; email access must be read-only, sending requires a separate permission.

nodes.label: Ghosting detection ('Possibly Ghosted', configurable threshold)
nodes.rationale: User sets Ghosted manually; the system should later suggest 'Possibly Ghosted' when no response and last activity exceeds a configurable threshold (30 days initially, never hard-coded). Later the company's historical response distribution may inform it.

nodes.label: POST /api/imports/csv (generic CSV import)
nodes.rationale: Required columns auto-detected via a TR/EN alias table (Company/Sirket, Title/Pozisyon, Applied At/Tarih); re-upload is idempotent (0 newApplications on second run).

nodes.label: Extension 'I Applied' flow (LinkedIn / kariyer.net -> application)
nodes.rationale: Popup best-effort scrapes company/title/location; all fields are editable before submit so an imperfect scrape never becomes a wrong submission.

nodes.label: activeTab + scripting permission justifications
nodes.rationale: Nothing runs until the toolbar click; the one-time script only reads title/company/location already visible on the page.

nodes.label: Data usage disclosure table and certifications
nodes.norm_label: data usage disclosure table and certifications
nodes.rationale: Based on what popup.js actually sends to POST /api/applications/from-extension and reads from GET /api/companies/search: auth info yes, website content yes, personal communications yes (opt-in only), PII/location/financial/health no.

nodes.label: Automation First principle
nodes.rationale: Minimize manual data entry: LinkedIn import, CSV import, Gmail/Outlook, browser extension and automatic status detection over time.

nodes.label: Scraping selectors are best-effort
nodes.rationale: Neither site's DOM class names are a stable API. kariyer.net selectors (scrapeKariyerNetJob) were verified live; LinkedIn's (scrapeLinkedInJob) were not. Breakage degrades to empty editable fields rather than wrong data; LinkedIn has a <title>-based fallback ('<Title> hiring at <Company> | LinkedIn').

nodes.label: Employment type not scraped, defaults to FullTime
nodes.norm_label: employment type not scraped, defaults to fulltime
nodes.rationale: LinkedIn's job header doesn't expose employment type directly, so created applications default to FullTime - same known limitation as generic CSV import (DECISIONS.md Sprint 4).

nodes.label: POST /api/applications/from-extension dedup by job URL
nodes.rationale: Clicking 'I Applied' again on the same job is safe: ApplicationService.CreateFromExtensionAsync dedupes by job URL and returns the existing application.

nodes.label: Extension Options page (API base URL, access token)
nodes.norm_label: extension options page (api base url, access token)

nodes.label: Extension popup page (popup.html)
nodes.rationale: Static shell with header (logo, open-options gear, language toggle, theme toggle) and a skeleton loading placeholder in #content; popup.js fills the real form after scraping.

nodes.label: scene-job.html popup-over-LinkedIn mockup
nodes.rationale: Reuses real popup.css classes (.app-header, .site-badge, label/input/button) so the mockup can't drift from the shipped popup; only the outer .popup-window frame is scene-specific. Theme is picked from ?theme= query param; a sun/moon icon matches theme.js.

nodes.label: Extension auth via aa_pat_ personal access token
nodes.norm_label: extension auth via aa_pat_ personal access token

nodes.label: Personal Access Token (Settings -> Browser Extension)
nodes.rationale: The extension authenticates with a PAT generated from /settings rather than the web app's JWT session, because an extension install has no browser session to share.

nodes.label: Gmail Scanning privacy terms (opt-in, on-device scoring)
nodes.norm_label: gmail scanning privacy terms (opt-in, on-device scoring)
nodes.rationale: Only the personally opened thread is read (capped at 2000 chars), scored on-device against a non-personal keyword/domain table; only qualifying emails send sender/subject/capped snippet; a local list of submitted thread IDs prevents duplicates.

nodes.label: User controls (revoke token, toggle scanning, uninstall)
nodes.norm_label: user controls (revoke token, toggle scanning, uninstall)

nodes.label: Extension theming (popup.css tokens mirror web Tailwind palette, theme.js)
nodes.norm_label: extension theming (popup.css tokens mirror web tailwind palette, theme.js)
nodes.rationale: popup.css mirrors web/src/components/ui/Button.tsx and Input.tsx so the extension reads as the same product; theme.js applies prefers-color-scheme by default and persists an explicit toggle per install via storage.js (no account sync - an extension install has no session).

nodes.label: Privacy policy URL required before submission
nodes.norm_label: privacy policy url required before submission
nodes.rationale: The Dashboard rejects submissions that handle authentication data (this extension stores a personal access token) without a privacy policy URL.

nodes.label: Scaled 1280x800 canvas + centered crop/upscale capture technique
nodes.norm_label: scaled 1280x800 canvas + centered crop/upscale capture technique
nodes.rationale: Each scene renders at a fixed 0.6 transform: scale() inside a flex-centered overflow:hidden viewport because screenshot tooling doesn't reliably honor a requested window size; the capture is recovered to exactly 1280x800 with sips centered crop (480x768) + upscale, which works because the canvas center coincides with the screenshot center.

nodes.label: Gmail Scanning (gmail-scan.js content script)
nodes.rationale: The only declared content_scripts entry because Gmail is a SPA with no full reload between inbox and thread, so click-triggered executeScript cannot detect a newly opened email. Off by default via the afterapply_gmail_scan_enabled flag; reads only the open thread (span[email], h2.hP, div.a3s capped at 2000 chars); POSTs an extracted signal, never the raw email, to /api/email-forwarding/extension-signal.

nodes.label: Chrome Web Store listing copy (EN/TR)
nodes.rationale: Item name 'e-kariyerim - Job Import' must match manifest.json's name exactly. Two language variants are added under Store listing -> Languages so Chrome localizes for Turkish visitors automatically. Category Productivity; icon reused from icons/icon128.png.

nodes.label: e-kariyerim API origin host permission justification
nodes.norm_label: e-kariyerim api origin host permission justification

nodes.label: Single-purpose description
nodes.rationale: Job-page capture and opt-in Gmail scanning are framed as one purpose - getting the user's own application activity into their own account - via two entry points, so the listing doesn't read as multiple unrelated features.

nodes.label: Chrome Web Store publishing checklist
nodes.rationale: The one manual step blocking submission is re-publishing the privacy policy at a real URL (its content became stale when Gmail Scanning was added); production host permissions/API URL and version bump are already done.

nodes.label: Store screenshot sources and regeneration
nodes.rationale: popup-light/dark.png and options-light.png (1280x800) are generated from scene-*.html marketing compositions that reuse popup.css's real classes with static sample data so they can't visually drift from the shipped pages.

nodes.label: Content scripts are plain scripts (no ES modules in MV3)
nodes.norm_label: content scripts are plain scripts (no es modules in mv3)
nodes.rationale: Chrome MV3 content scripts have no import/export support, so gmail-scan.js and local-filter-config.js duplicate the bit of chrome.storage.local logic they need instead of importing storage.js.

nodes.label: Forward-all-inbox design removed; extension signal is sole email intake
nodes.norm_label: forward-all-inbox design removed; extension signal is sole email intake
nodes.rationale: The earlier forward-all-inbox design (EmailProvider.Forwarding, Gmail forwarding guide page, Cloudflare Email Worker) was removed after live testing showed it and Gmail-filter alternatives couldn't stay both bounded and complete. The /api/email-forwarding route namespace stays for compatibility with installed extension versions; EmailProvider now has a single member, Extension.

nodes.label: host_permissions must list the API origin
nodes.norm_label: host_permissions must list the api origin
nodes.rationale: A Manifest V3 extension page's fetch() is exempt from CORS only for origins explicitly listed in host_permissions; an unlisted API origin is blocked like an ordinary cross-origin fetch (found via manual testing, DECISIONS.md Sprint 9).

nodes.label: local-filter-config.js (ETag-cached scoring vocabulary)
nodes.rationale: Fetches the vocabulary from GET /api/email-forwarding/local-filter-config with ETag revalidation so tuning weights/phrases/domains only needs an appsettings.json edit + backend redeploy, never a new extension release; small bundled fallback for first-run/offline.

nodes.label: afterApplyScoreSignal local scoring (mirror of RecruitmentSignalAnalyzer)
nodes.rationale: A JS mirror of the backend's RecruitmentSignalAnalyzer.Analyze shape (weighted phrase-category hits, capped, plus known-domain/link-domain bonuses) runs in the browser so only threads above the threshold are ever sent.

nodes.label: Re-check Privacy practices tab after permission change
nodes.norm_label: re-check privacy practices tab after permission change
nodes.rationale: A permission whose justification doesn't match its actual use is one of the most common rejection reasons, and the Gmail host permission + content script is the biggest permission change since the first draft.

nodes.label: manifest version 0.5.0 bump for Gmail Scanning; bump per upload
nodes.norm_label: manifest version 0.5.0 bump for gmail scanning; bump per upload
nodes.rationale: 0.4.0 -> 0.5.0 for the new mail.google.com host permission + first declared content_scripts entry; the Dashboard rejects a re-upload with an already-used version.

nodes.label: Email worker bounded webhook retry (historical, worker deleted)
nodes.norm_label: email worker bounded webhook retry (historical, worker deleted)
nodes.rationale: Throwing from email() would bounce mail to recruiters, worse than silent loss.

nodes.label: Cross-border Transfer Disclosure (Email → OpenAI)
nodes.rationale: Covers both intake paths sharing the OpenAI pipeline; no granular consent checkbox added yet.

nodes.label: EmailSuggestion Subject/Snippet Persisted (body never)
nodes.rationale: Earlier checklist wrongly claimed subject/snippet were memory-only; corrected 2026-09-02.

nodes.label: Gmail Scanning via Extension (EmailProvider.Extension)
nodes.rationale: Relevance scored on-device; only sender/subject/short snippet above threshold reach the server.

nodes.label: Open Gap: no granular consent for email → OpenAI
nodes.norm_label: open gap: no granular consent for email → openai

nodes.label: KVKK / GDPR Self-review Checklist
nodes.rationale: Engineering self-review, not legal advice; must be updated when features change.

nodes.label: Consent persisted server-side (ConsentAcceptedAt)
nodes.rationale: A frontend-only checkbox is not provable.

nodes.label: Email forwarding (forward-all-inbox) removed; Gmail Scanning sole intake (2026-09-03)
nodes.norm_label: email forwarding (forward-all-inbox) removed; gmail scanning sole intake (2026-09-03)
nodes.rationale: Provider-agnostic suggestion pipeline kept; /api/email-forwarding route and class names kept as historical identifiers.

nodes.label: Email subject/snippet → OpenAI disclosure on /privacy
nodes.rationale: Disclosure only; a granular consent checkbox is a separate product decision.

nodes.label: Google Sign-in Data (sub, verified email, name)
nodes.norm_label: google sign-in data (sub, verified email, name)
nodes.rationale: Only ID token identity read; no Google access/refresh token stored; non-sensitive scopes, no CASA.

nodes.label: Data-flow Inventory and Open Legal Items
nodes.norm_label: data-flow inventory and open legal items

nodes.label: AI Job Matching: hidden → reopened with consent → fully removed (2026-09-02)
nodes.norm_label: ai job matching: hidden → reopened with consent → fully removed (2026-09-02)
nodes.rationale: Sending CV text to OpenAI was the most critical KVKK gap; the feature was ultimately cut from product scope. OpenAI email classifiers kept, OpenAiOptions moved.

nodes.label: Anonymous GET /api/config (password policy, PAT limits, googleAuth.enabled)
nodes.norm_label: anonymous get /api/config (password policy, pat limits, googleauth.enabled)
nodes.rationale: Reads IOptions<IdentityOptions> so FE shows exactly what the server enforces; excluded from auth rate limit.

nodes.label: CompanyIntelligence:Enabled flag (404 when off)
nodes.rationale: First boolean feature flag; 404 hides even company existence; service tested via DI with flag off.

nodes.label: Feature-flag pattern: disabled endpoints answer 404
nodes.rationale: Flag existence is not observable from outside (not 403, not empty 200).

nodes.label: Gmail OAuth integration removed from code (2026-08-31)
nodes.norm_label: gmail oauth integration removed from code (2026-08-31)
nodes.rationale: gmail.readonly is a restricted scope requiring CASA assessment (~$15k-75k, 4-12 weeks); investment declined.

nodes.label: Google ID token: no signature verification (OIDC Core 3.1.3.7 step 6)
nodes.norm_label: google id token: no signature verification (oidc core 3.1.3.7 step 6)
nodes.rationale: Token arrives server-to-server over TLS from the token endpoint; browser-sourced tokens must never pass through this reader.

nodes.label: Sign in with Google: authorization code + PKCE, server-side exchange
nodes.norm_label: sign in with google: authorization code + pkce, server-side exchange
nodes.rationale: Google Identity Services rejected because it needs CSP loosening; PKCE also provides login-CSRF defense.

nodes.label: Bug: /api/config cached without Vary: Origin hid Google button
nodes.norm_label: bug: /api/config cached without vary: origin hid google button
nodes.rationale: Chrome cached a no-CORS-headers copy for 5 minutes after the dev opened the URL directly.

nodes.label: Data-gated Phases (infra built, activation flag-gated)
nodes.rationale: Company Intelligence and CES need other users aggregate data; cannot be finished without real users.

nodes.label: Launch Strategy: full product, not incremental MVP
nodes.norm_label: launch strategy: full product, not incremental mvp
nodes.rationale: No time pressure since launch is postponed, so more phases can be finished before first release.

nodes.label: Single GET /api/analytics/overview endpoint
nodes.rationale: Three spec endpoints would triple DB round-trips for one dashboard section.

nodes.label: ApplicationStatusClassification moved to Domain
nodes.rationale: One definition of responded/interview/offer shared by Analytics and CompanyIntelligence.

nodes.label: Background Jobs: Hangfire (Postgres-backed)
nodes.rationale: Built-in retry meets the spec retry-safe requirement.

nodes.label: CompanyGivenClosureStatuses {Rejected, Accepted}
nodes.rationale: Terminal set counts Ghosted as closed, which CES must penalize; Withdrawn is candidate-driven.

nodes.label: Company Intelligence computed on-read, no aggregate table
nodes.norm_label: company intelligence computed on-read, no aggregate table
nodes.rationale: Premature optimization with zero users; cached aggregate is a later sprint.

nodes.label: Cross-user query: single isolated exception for background jobs
nodes.norm_label: cross-user query: single isolated exception for background jobs
nodes.rationale: ScanAndGenerateRemindersAsync has no ClaimsPrincipal; not a precedent for other services.

nodes.label: Hangfire schema separate from EF migrations
nodes.norm_label: hangfire schema separate from ef migrations

nodes.label: Product metrics: daily Hangfire job + structured log, no dashboard
nodes.norm_label: product metrics: daily hangfire job + structured log, no dashboard

nodes.label: Persistent Reminder entity (Notifications module)
nodes.rationale: Gives Hangfire a real retryable job; dismissable state; idempotent via unique index.

nodes.label: Responded definition is history-based
nodes.rationale: Applied→Screening→Ghosted still counts as responded; Withdrawn and Ghosted excluded.

nodes.label: Shared TerminalApplicationStatuses (concrete HashSet)
nodes.rationale: EF Core only translates Contains on concrete collection types, not IReadOnlySet.

nodes.label: Local prod-like Docker Compose Profile
nodes.rationale: Sprint 7 stand-in for a real deploy; deliberately no reverse proxy/TLS or secrets manager (YAGNI without a cloud target).

nodes.label: Sprint 7 — MVP Hardening and Private Beta
nodes.norm_label: sprint 7 — mvp hardening and private beta
nodes.rationale: Added because the spec never turned privacy/legal and product metrics into a sprint.

nodes.label: Sprint 12 B2B employer dashboard removed from roadmap
nodes.norm_label: sprint 12 b2b employer dashboard removed from roadmap
nodes.rationale: No real employer demand; speculative far-future design.

nodes.label: Domain does not model User (plain Guid UserId)
nodes.norm_label: domain does not model user (plain guid userid)
nodes.rationale: IdentityUser would violate layer tests; no domain behaviour on User yet (YAGNI).

nodes.label: Email verification at registration deferred (Resend free quota)
nodes.norm_label: email verification at registration deferred (resend free quota)
nodes.rationale: 100 emails/day reserved for password reset; verification mail could starve reset flow. Squatting risk accepted while small.

nodes.label: Google account auto-link by verified email
nodes.norm_label: google account auto-link by verified email
nodes.rationale: email_verified=false rejected; unverified password accounts could still be linked (same squatting class).

nodes.label: Modular Monolith, Layer-first (4 projects)
nodes.rationale: Modules live as namespaces inside each layer; NetArchTest guards cross-module dependencies.

nodes.label: YAGNI / no speculative infrastructure
nodes.rationale: Recurring principle: no MediatR, no domain User, no reverse proxy without a target, no dashboards without users.

nodes.label: MVP: Job Application Tracker + Personal Analytics
nodes.norm_label: mvp: job application tracker + personal analytics
nodes.rationale: MVP is explicitly not Company Intelligence, AI assistant or B2B. Success = a user uploads LinkedIn export, hundreds of applications imported and deduped, dashboard/status/timeline/rates visible, without a spreadsheet. 'Wow moment' is the LinkedIn export becoming a dashboard in minutes. LLM must not be a required dependency in MVP.

nodes.label: Turkiye-first, global-ready market strategy
nodes.rationale: First wedge is Turkish white-collar tech professionals (high LinkedIn use, many online applications, founder knows the segment). Domain model must stay global from day one (Country, Currency, Language, Timezone, EmploymentType, RemoteType) even though MVP UX is Turkish.

nodes.label: North Star metric: Verified Application Outcomes
nodes.norm_label: north star metric: verified application outcomes
nodes.rationale: Long-term value comes from quality outcome data, not application count alone.

nodes.label: Postman collection as a generated build artifact
nodes.norm_label: postman collection as a generated build artifact
nodes.rationale: Only environments/*.json are hand-maintained; collection.json is regenerated from the API's OpenAPI document by npm run generate, which layers in bearer auth wired to {{accessToken}}, login/register/refresh test scripts, and a baseline status-code + JSON content-type assertion per request.

nodes.label: Backend First principle
nodes.rationale: The MVP's value lies in the data model, application lifecycle, analytics and automation; avoid unnecessary UI complexity.

nodes.label: Candidate First principle
nodes.rationale: The first user is the job seeker; employer analytics is a later phase.

nodes.label: Claude Code working rules (20 engineering rules)
nodes.norm_label: claude code working rules (20 engineering rules)
nodes.rationale: Stay in MVP scope, no microservices, simple working solution first, design domain for future analytics, privacy-first, tests on every important change, open API contracts, versioned migrations, no hard-coded config, abstract external providers, idempotency, retry-safe jobs, no user data in logs, no unnecessary email persistence, YAGNI, and record open product decisions in DECISIONS.md for user approval.

nodes.label: Data flywheel and long-term moat
nodes.rationale: Tracker is the product entry point; application outcome data is the long-term moat. More users -> more applications -> more verified outcomes -> better company intelligence -> more users. Architecture must serve both user value (tracking) and network value (anonymous aggregate hiring intelligence).

nodes.label: Modular Monolith + Clean Architecture (.NET 10, PostgreSQL, Redis)
nodes.norm_label: modular monolith + clean architecture (.net 10, postgresql, redis)
nodes.rationale: Do not start with microservices; single deployable with Identity/Applications/Companies/Jobs/Imports/Analytics/Notifications modules. Hangfire or hosted services for background jobs; REST + OpenAPI; Docker; no unnecessary cloud abstraction.

nodes.label: postman/openapi/openapi.json emitted at dotnet build
nodes.rationale: AfterApply.Api.csproj's OpenApiDocumentsDirectory and DependencyInjection.IsOpenApiDocumentGeneration run Program.cs route registration through a mock server, so no live Postgres/Redis is needed to emit the document.

nodes.label: Clean Architecture, layer-first modular monolith
nodes.rationale: Modules (Applications, Companies, Jobs, Identity, Imports, Analytics, Notifications, CompanyIntelligence) live as namespaces/folders inside each layer, not separate projects (DECISIONS.md #1). Layer direction Domain <- Application <- Infrastructure <- Api is enforced by NetArchTest in tests/AfterApply.UnitTests/Architecture.

nodes.label: deploy-web Job (afterapply-web)
nodes.rationale: No Cloud SQL/VPC flags: web only talks to the API over HTTPS.

nodes.label: notify-deploy (Slack #deployments)
nodes.rationale: Single combined message; skipped when count is 0 (redeploy of same SHA).

nodes.label: Deploy Plan Job (diff each side against last successful deploy tag)
nodes.norm_label: deploy plan job (diff each side against last successful deploy tag)
nodes.rationale: Diffing the push range stranded never-deployed changes after a failed deploy; diffing against the tag asks what changed since what is live.

nodes.label: Deploy backend and web independently (push:main + target input)
nodes.norm_label: deploy backend and web independently (push:main + target input)
nodes.rationale: workflow_dispatch cannot pick a single job; most changes touch one side.

nodes.label: Deploy Slack notification with commits since last successful deploy
nodes.norm_label: deploy slack notification with commits since last successful deploy
nodes.rationale: High-water-mark tag captures intervening pushes that never deployed.

nodes.label: Plan job diffs against deploy/*-latest tags, not push range
nodes.norm_label: plan job diffs against deploy/*-latest tags, not push range
nodes.rationale: A CI-only fix push skipped deploys and stranded the Google sign-in rollout; failed deploys do not move the tag.

nodes.label: First-deploy Bootstrap Order (backend → web → CORS loop)
nodes.norm_label: first-deploy bootstrap order (backend → web → cors loop)
nodes.rationale: deploy-web needs the API URL baked in, and CORS needs the web URL; one-time two-run dance.

nodes.label: Post-deploy Smoke Verification (/health + register 201)
nodes.rationale: A green deploy is not proof; the first real deploy 500ed on registration because migrations were skipped.

nodes.label: Cloud Provider: everything on Google Cloud
nodes.norm_label: cloud provider: everything on google cloud
nodes.rationale: User opened a GCP trial and wanted one provider; Cloud SQL and Memorystore cost money after the trial, stated openly.

nodes.label: Redis added though unused by business logic
nodes.norm_label: redis added though unused by business logic
nodes.rationale: Rate limiting is in-memory; only the health check touches Redis. Kept for future cache/distributed limiting, cost accepted.

nodes.label: Error tracking: Sentry (.NET + Next.js)
nodes.rationale: Empty DSN silently disables the SDK, so no placeholder pattern is used.

nodes.label: Sprint 13 real deploy findings (403 private, missing migrations, broken secret paste)
nodes.norm_label: sprint 13 real deploy findings (403 private, missing migrations, broken secret paste)

nodes.label: Cloudflare DNS-only for Certificate Issuance
nodes.rationale: A proxied record layers one TLS terminator in front of another and breaks Google cert provisioning.

nodes.label: GCP Cost Note (Cloud SQL + Memorystore not free after trial)
nodes.norm_label: gcp cost note (cloud sql + memorystore not free after trial)

nodes.label: Make Cloud Run Services Public (allUsers run.invoker)
nodes.norm_label: make cloud run services public (allusers run.invoker)
nodes.rationale: New services are private by default; Google recommends CI/CD not manage this, so it is a manual one-time step.

nodes.label: API draft (applications, companies, jobs, imports, analytics)
nodes.norm_label: api draft (applications, companies, jobs, imports, analytics)

nodes.label: Company entity model and name normalization
nodes.norm_label: company entity model and name normalization
nodes.rationale: Company identity must be normalized (ABC Teknoloji / ABC Technology / ABC Tech resolve to one); simple normalization suffices for MVP, fuzzy matching / external identity resolution later.

nodes.label: Job entity model (Source + ExternalId)
nodes.rationale: Source + ExternalId (e.g. LinkedIn / 4449445627) identifies whether the same posting was applied to before.

nodes.label: LinkedIn Data Export import pipeline
nodes.rationale: The MVP's key differentiator: Upload ZIP -> find Jobs/Job Applications*.csv -> parse -> normalize -> resolve company/job -> deduplicate -> create -> summary. Must be idempotent.

nodes.label: Personal Analytics (response/interview/offer/ghosting rates, response time)

nodes.label: JobPostingSourceResolver (Job.Source / Job.ExternalId vs Application.Source)

nodes.label: AI Job Matching setup (OpenAI:ApiKey)
nodes.rationale: Ships with an obvious placeholder key so the feature is structurally complete but inert; no automated test calls the real OpenAI API - persist/cache logic is tested against a fake IJobMatchingProvider.

nodes.label: Container environment (podman/docker compose)
nodes.rationale: Dev compose only runs Postgres/Redis/API (no frontend container); host ports offset to 5434/6382 to avoid collisions with native or other-project containers. Fully containerized run uses the docker-compose.prod.yml overlay.

nodes.label: Google Sign-In setup (authorization code + PKCE)
nodes.rationale: Plain redirect to accounts.google.com with no Google script on the page keeps the web app's CSP untouched; the API (GoogleAuthClient) exchanges the code server-side and only reads the ID token with openid/email/profile scopes so no Google app verification is needed. App:WebBaseUrl must be the redirect-URI origin - the API refuses any other origin before calling Google. GoogleSignInTests runs the flow against a fake IGoogleAuthClient.

nodes.label: Offset host ports 5434/6382
nodes.rationale: Native Homebrew Postgres owns 5432 and 5433/6379 are taken by another local project's containers, so the compose file publishes 5434 and 6382 instead.

nodes.label: ports: !override [] to clear dev-published DB ports
nodes.norm_label: ports: !override [] to clear dev-published db ports
nodes.rationale: Compose merges list fields by concatenation, so an empty list would be a no-op appended to the dev file's ports; !override is required to actually remove the published port.

nodes.label: docker-compose.prod.yml prod-like overlay
nodes.rationale: Not a real cloud deployment - a locally verifiable stand-in for the Sprint 7 DoD ('prod-benzeri ortam') while cloud provider selection was open. Postgres/Redis stop publishing host ports, the API keeps its host port (no reverse proxy), a Next.js web service is added, and all secrets come from git-ignored .env.prod.

nodes.label: Empty Sentry__Dsn disables the SDK (no placeholder)
nodes.norm_label: empty sentry__dsn disables the sdk (no placeholder)
nodes.rationale: Unlike OpenAI/Resend REPLACE_WITH_ placeholders, a fake Sentry DSN would make the SDK try and fail to send an event on every request instead of silently no-op'ing, so the default is empty.

nodes.label: RateLimiting__Auth__PermitLimit override for CI contract check
nodes.norm_label: ratelimiting__auth__permitlimit override for ci contract check
nodes.rationale: Default is the real policy (5/min per IP). CI's API contract check fires every /api/auth/* request back to back from one IP via the Postman collection, so the 6th would 429 for reasons unrelated to the contract - the env var lets CI raise it.

nodes.label: Connection strings from config chain, fail fast if unset
nodes.norm_label: connection strings from config chain, fail fast if unset
nodes.rationale: No connection string is hard-coded; ConnectionStrings:Postgres/Redis come from user-secrets locally or ConnectionStrings__* env vars in compose. If unset the API fails on startup with an explanatory error rather than silently connecting to the wrong database.

nodes.label: External integrations are inert until configured
nodes.norm_label: external integrations are inert until configured
nodes.rationale: OpenAI, Resend and Google Auth all follow the same pattern: with secrets unset, GET /api/config reports the feature disabled, the UI hides the entry point, and the endpoints answer 404. Avoids half-configured features misbehaving in environments that lack the secret.

nodes.label: Account deletion: app-level orchestration, no DB FK on UserId
nodes.norm_label: account deletion: app-level orchestration, no db fk on userid

nodes.label: RuleBasedEmailClassifier (rejection wins on conflict)

nodes.rationale: required is not enforced by the binder and bound ints cannot distinguish 0 from missing.

nodes.label: Google signupToken (separate audience + purpose claim, 10 min)
nodes.norm_label: google signuptoken (separate audience + purpose claim, 10 min)

nodes.label: Stateless OAuth state as signed JWT with purpose claim
nodes.norm_label: stateless oauth state as signed jwt with purpose claim
nodes.rationale: Reuses Jwt:SigningKey; purpose claim stops access tokens being replayed as state.

nodes.label: Passwordless Google accounts (HasPassword, optional delete password)
nodes.norm_label: passwordless google accounts (haspassword, optional delete password)

nodes.label: Personal Access Token design (unscoped v1, SHA-256 hashed, aa_pat_ prefix)
nodes.norm_label: personal access token design (unscoped v1, sha-256 hashed, aa_pat_ prefix)
nodes.rationale: Endpoint allow-lists risked silently open endpoints; user-generated credential accepted unscoped like GitHub classic PATs.

nodes.label: PAT Scope + 90-day expiry enforced via default authorization policy
nodes.norm_label: pat scope + 90-day expiry enforced via default authorization policy
nodes.rationale: Enforcing in the default policy keeps new endpoints closed to extension tokens unless explicitly allowed.

nodes.label: RecruitmentSignalAnalyzer (score gate replaces isKnownSender hard gate)
nodes.norm_label: recruitmentsignalanalyzer (score gate replaces isknownsender hard gate)
nodes.rationale: Rule classifier already ran unconditionally; the gap was paraphrased text and categories without rules. Phrase lists intentionally broader than the classifier.

nodes.label: SmartBearer policy scheme forwarding (JWT vs PAT)

nodes.rationale: Same Authorization header; no RequireAuthorization call changed.

nodes.label: Token storage: localStorage + single-flight refresh
nodes.rationale: Single-flight prevents concurrent refreshes from triggering reuse-detection revocation; no cross-tab sync.
